Answer: B
Reason: The lateral view (Figure 4b) confirms the mass is located in the anterior mediastinum (retrosternal space), and the frontal view shows a lobulated, widened mediastinal silhouette with ill-defined margins. These features, combined with the history of sternotomy (suggesting prior intervention or aggressive disease), are most consistent with a malignant thymic carcinoma rather than a benign cyst or well-encapsulated thymoma.
